title: Mold Remediation Software: Reports, Scheduling and Billing Tools
html:
Mold remediation software has to produce a record you can defend: photos, readings, scope and a signed job. Start with a documentation tool such as Encircle or CompanyCam, add a scheduling and invoicing app, and build a website that wins urgent searches. Published prices in this guide run from $19 to $583 a month, and Albiware does not publish a price.

Mold remediation software earns its keep on paperwork. A mold job runs on an inspection, a written protocol, containment photos and a clearance result. When a homeowner, a realtor or an insurer questions the work, the file is your proof.

This guide sorts tools by the part of the job they protect: documentation, scheduling, forms and billing. Each tool shows the price its own vendor lists and one real limit.

Which mold remediation software documents the job best?

Encircle and CompanyCam both document a job from a phone, but they solve different problems. One is built for restoration files, and the other is a general project photo tool.

  • Encircle: lists field documentation, floor plans, moisture records and a scope to estimate step that exports to Xactimate. Field documentation is $285 a month and field documentation with scope to estimate is $583 a month on monthly billing. Limit: plans carry a 12-month term and are priced by yearly job volume, and the page does not say which tier the price covers.
  • CompanyCam: stores timestamped photos by project, builds reports and collects payment on site. Core is $63 a month billed annually, Crew is $129 and Scale is $199, with extra users at $29. Limit: Core includes one user and caps at two, and the page lists no mold-specific templates.

Pick by what your clients ask for. If insurers request a scope and a moisture record, a restoration tool such as Encircle fits. If most of your work is private-pay remediation with a photo report, a photo tool may be enough.

Whichever you choose, set a photo standard. Shoot each room before containment, the containment build, the affected materials, the removal and the finished surface. Name shots by room and date so a reader who never visited the site can follow the story.

Which software manages a mold remediation company from call to payment?

Albiware is a restoration job management platform, and Jobber and Housecall Pro are general field service apps. They sit at different price points and cover different amounts of the job.

  • Albiware: its site lists restoration job management, field documentation, drying logs, a CRM and payments. The page does not mention mold by name. Limit: its prices are not public.
  • Jobber: Core is $49 a month with no commitment or $29 a month billed annually, for one user. Extra users cost $29 a month each. Limit: card payments cost 2.9% plus 30 cents.
  • Housecall Pro: Basic is $59 a month billed annually or $79 monthly for one user. Essentials is $149 or $189 for five users. Max is $299 or $329 for eight users. Limit: many add-ons show no price on the page.

A small remediation company with a few jobs a week can run Jobber for scheduling, quotes and invoices, and CompanyCam for the record. A larger firm that works with insurers and tracks drying should ask Albiware for a quote and compare it with Encircle.

What forms and checklists should a mold remediation company standardize?

Standard forms protect you, and software only helps if the forms exist. Decide the paperwork first, then pick the tool that stores it.

  • Pre-job: signed work authorization, a written scope and a note of the moisture source found.
  • Containment: a checklist for barriers, negative air and photos before demolition.
  • Daily log: work done, materials removed and equipment placed, signed by the lead.
  • Clearance: a place to attach the clearance result and the date the area was released.
  • Closeout: final photos, a customer sign-off and a warranty note if you offer one.

Contractor Foreman lists forms and checklists, custom templates and inspections among its project tools. On monthly billing, Standard is $139 for up to three users and Plus is $199 for up to eight. Limit: Basic is offered on annual billing only.

Ask any vendor to load your own checklist during the demo, and have the crew lead try it on a phone. A form that is slow to fill in the field gets skipped. If it takes more than an afternoon, the tool will be a burden for the crew.

What do small mold crews use for estimates, invoices and the books?

A small crew can keep billing simple with a light estimate app and an accounting package.

  • Joist: Basics is $10 a month and Pro is $17 a month on monthly billing. Elite is $32 and Run is $100. Limit: Basics allows 5 documents a month.
  • QuickBooks Online: Simple Start is $19 a month for the first three months, then $38. Essentials is $42.50, then $85, and Plus is $70, then $140. Limit: users are capped at one, three and five by plan.

Write estimates with a line for each phase: containment, removal, cleaning, drying and rebuild. Homeowners accept a scope they can read, and insurers expect the same breakdown.

Taking a deposit before containment starts is common practice for remediation work. It keeps the crew from building barriers for a job that never closes. Choose a tool that can collect it online and attach it to the job.

Which tools bring in mold remediation calls?

Software runs the job, but calls come from search, maps and ads. Google states that creating a Business Profile is free, so a complete profile is the cheapest lead tool a remediation company can own.

Limit: a profile needs photos, accurate service areas and replies to every review.

Mold searches are urgent and often follow a bad smell or a leak, so ads can fill a schedule fast. See the pricing page .

How do you choose mold remediation software for your company?

Choose mold remediation software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Cost: add the plan, extra users, term length, job-volume tiers and card fees, then compare with the margin on one average job.

Setup effort: can your lead load your forms and a price list in one week without paid training?

Company typeStarting stackAdd next
Owner and one crewCompanyCam Core, Jobber Core, QuickBooks Simple Start, free Business ProfileForms and checklists
Two to four crews, private payCompanyCam Crew, Housecall Pro Essentials or Jobber Connect, QuickBooks EssentialsRestoration file system
Insurer work and drying recordsEncircle or Albiware, QuickBooks PlusMarketing support for lead flow

A one-crew shop should keep the stack short and strict. A larger company should pilot a tool on one live job and compare the report with your current one before committing to a 12-month term.

Software does not create demand. A website with a page for each service, such as inspection, removal and crawl space work, turns urgent searches into calls.

What do mold remediation owners get wrong when they buy software?

The first error is buying a restoration suite for a three-person crew. A 12-month term at Encircle pricing is a real commitment, so match the tool to your job volume.

The second error is skipping the exit plan. Ask how to export photos, reports and forms if you cancel, and what format they come in.

The third error is relying on software for compliance. A tool stores what you capture. It does not know your state rules, so confirm licensing and protocol requirements with your regulator and your insurer.

What should a mold remediation job file contain?

A complete job file lets anyone reconstruct the job without calling the crew. Build the file structure first, then check that your tool stores each item.

  • Intake: the homeowner request, the symptoms reported and the date of first contact.
  • Assessment: the moisture source, affected areas and any test results from the assessor.
  • Scope and price: the written protocol, the estimate and the signed authorization.
  • Work record: daily logs, photos at each stage and equipment placed.
  • Release: the clearance result, closeout photos and the customer sign-off.
  • Billing: deposit, invoices, payments and any change orders.

Check whether the tool lets a homeowner, a realtor or an adjuster view the file without paying for a seat. Shared links save hours of emailing PDFs.

Also test retrieval. Pick a job from last year and try to find the clearance result in under a minute. If you cannot, the tool will not help when a dispute arrives.

How should you price mold remediation work in your software?

Price in phases so the homeowner and the insurer can see where the money goes. Software makes this easy when each phase is a saved line item.

Set up separate items for containment, removal, cleaning, air filtration and rebuild. Add a clear note on what is excluded, such as repairs to the leak source, since a remediation scope rarely covers the plumbing fix.

Keep unit prices in the tool and review them each quarter. Labor, disposal and equipment rental change, and old prices leak margin. When a job runs over, record why on the job so the next estimate learns from it.

Finally, decide how you handle change orders. Hidden mold found behind a wall is common, so a signed change order form attached to the job protects both sides. Choose a tool that can send and store that form on a phone.

What software does a mold remediation company need?

A mold remediation company needs photo documentation, forms, scheduling, invoicing and payment tools. Start with a photo report app, a scheduling app and a free Google Business Profile. Add a restoration file system when insurer work and drying records grow.

How much does mold remediation software cost?

Published prices in this guide start at $19 a month for QuickBooks Simple Start and $29 a month for Jobber Core billed annually. CompanyCam Core is $63 billed annually, and Encircle lists $285 to $583 a month. Albiware does not publish a price, so ask the vendor.

Is Encircle worth it for a mold remediation company?

It fits companies that work with insurers and need moisture records and a scope that exports to Xactimate. It lists $285 a month for documentation on a 12-month term. A small private-pay crew may do better with CompanyCam at $63 billed annually.

Does Albiware work for mold remediation?

Albiware presents itself as restoration job management software, with documentation, drying logs, a CRM and payments. Ask for a demo using one of your own mold jobs.

Can Jobber run a mold remediation business?

Jobber handles scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so it suits small crews. Core is $49 a month with no commitment or $29 billed annually for one user. It does not replace a documentation tool, so pair it with a photo app and your own forms.

Do mold remediation companies need a website if they use job software?

Yes. Job software runs the work after the call, but it does not bring calls in. A website with pages for inspection, removal and prevention, plus a Google Business Profile with reviews, gives worried homeowners a reason to call you first.

It fits companies that work with insurers and need moisture records and a scope that exports to Xactimate. It lists $285 a month for documentation on a 12-month term. A small private-pay crew may do better with CompanyCam at $63 billed annually.
###
Does Albiware work for mold remediation?
Albiware presents itself as restoration job management software, with documentation, drying logs, a CRM and payments. Ask for a demo using one of your own mold jobs.
###
Can Jobber run a mold remediation business?
Jobber handles scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments, so it suits small crews. Core is $49 a month with no commitment or $29 billed annually for one user. It does not replace a documentation tool, so pair it with a photo app and your own forms.
###
Do mold remediation companies need a website if they use job software?
Yes. Job software runs the work after the call, but it does not bring calls in. A website with pages for inspection, removal and prevention, plus a Google Business Profile with reviews, gives worried homeowners a reason to call you first.
